title: Princess Diana was betrayed TWICE... and never knew about the second
note: True story: Diana's 1995 Panorama interview and the 2021 Dyson inquiry. Panorama footage appears only inside news reports (Channel 4 News, ITV News, Sky, ABC), never as a raw re-upload: the BBC won't license it and Prince William asked it never be aired. 'The inquiry found'; Dyson's caveat and Diana's 'no regrets' note included. Earl Spencer's death-link line deliberately left out. Script: diana_betrayed_twice.script.md.

beats.say: In 1995, Princess Diana told the world her marriage had been betrayed. Twenty-six years later, we found out she had been betrayed again, by the people who filmed her saying it.
beats.speak: In nineteen ninety-five, Princess Diana told the world her marriage had been betrayed. Twenty-six years later, we found out she had been betrayed again, by the people who filmed her saying it.

beats.say: She married Prince Charles in 1981, at twenty. An estimated seven hundred and fifty million people watched.
beats.speak: She married Prince Charles in nineteen eighty-one, at twenty. An estimated seven hundred and fifty million people watched.

beats.say: But the marriage fell apart. In 1994, Charles admitted on TV that he had been unfaithful, once the marriage had, in his words, irretrievably broken down.
beats.speak: But the marriage fell apart. In nineteen ninety-four, Charles admitted on TV that he had been unfaithful, once the marriage had, in his words, irretrievably broken down.

beats.say: A year later, Diana gave her answer, in a secret BBC interview. Nearly twenty-three million people watched.
It became one of the most famous interviews ever. The reporter, Martin Bashir, became a star.
But years later, questions surfaced about how he got it.

In 2021, an official inquiry found that Bashir had commissioned fake bank statements, suggesting people close to Diana were being paid to spy on her. He showed them to her brother, and that led to his meeting with Diana.
beats.speak: In twenty twenty-one, an official inquiry found that Bashir had commissioned fake bank statements, suggesting people close to Diana were being paid to spy on her. He showed them to her brother, and that led to his meeting with Diana.

beats.say: The inquiry called it deceitful behaviour. Worse, it found the BBC's own investigation in 1996 was woefully ineffective, and the truth stayed buried for twenty-five years.
beats.speak: The inquiry called it deceitful behaviour. Worse, it found the BBC's own investigation in nineteen ninety-six was woefully ineffective, and the truth stayed buried for twenty-five years.

beats.say: To be fair, the inquiry also said Diana would probably have agreed to an interview anyway. And Bashir said the documents had no bearing on her decision.
The BBC apologised, gave the money from the interview to charity, and promised never to show it again.
Diana never knew. She died in Paris in 1997, two years after the interview.
beats.speak: Diana never knew. She died in Paris in nineteen ninety-seven, two years after the interview.

beats.say: So the most famous interview she ever gave, a story about betrayal, was itself built on a betrayal.
